# Thanksgiving Table Decor: Place Cards, Placemats, and Runners to Make with Cricut


-
-
-


19 November 2026


[Beth Baty](https://cricut.com/blog/author/bethb/)


---


A few personalized pieces can pull your whole Thanksgiving table together. A name at each seat, a runner with a favorite phrase, and matching napkin rings make the gathering feel special before the first dish has even arrived.


With Cricut, you can make Thanksgiving place cards, placemats, table runners, napkin rings, and glass tags. Start with a color palette you love, repeat a leaf or pumpkin design across a few projects, and use the dishes and linens you already have to keep the prep simple while still ending with an elevated, cozy vibe.


## How to set a Thanksgiving table


Build your Thanksgiving table one layer at a time. This setup works for a relaxed family meal or a Friendsgiving dinner, with room to add your own handmade details. Plus, find design ideas for the projects mentioned in this how-to guide after the step-by-step tutorial!


### 1. Start with a runner or tablecloth


If you’d prefer to use a tablecloth, lay that down first. Otherwise, you can skip straight to draping a personalized Thanksgiving table runner along the center of the table. Don’t forget to leave space for serving dishes if you’re passing food family-style!


### 2. Add placemats and plates


Set a custom Thanksgiving placemat at each seat. Doing so looks elegant and protects your table or nice tablecloth from spills!


While nicer cardstock or fabric placemats are best for adults, coloring placemats make more sense for the kids’ table and keep all the kids busy while they’re waiting on food.


### 3. Arrange plates, silverware, and napkins


Center each plate on its placemat, with forks on the left and the knife and spoon on the right. Don’t forget to turn the knife blade toward the plate!


Place each napkin on the plate or folded beside the fork. A handmade napkin ring can incorporate your themed colors or design motifs, and if you know how to fold a napkin in a fun way, this could be a fun place to showcase that!


### 4. Set out glassware and glass tags


Place water glasses above the knives on the right side. Personalized glass tags help everyone keep track of their drink beyond dinner and throughout the night, and they can be used in place of traditional name place cards.


### 5. Position place cards


If you’ve decided to use traditional name place cards, be sure to set the Thanksgiving place cards above each plate or tuck them into each napkin ring where the name is easy to see.


### 6. Finish with the centerpiece


Add a Thanksgiving centerpiece that leaves room for conversation and the meal. Sit down for a quick check to be sure that everyone can see across the table and no one’s view is obstructed by the centerpiece!


## Thanksgiving table decor you can make with Cricut


Start by choosing just one project to personalize each seat with, then add other details after, if you have time. Using the same lettering or fall shape (such as a leaf, pumpkin, or turkey silhouette) across all of your projects makes it easy to coordinate and keeps everything cohesive.


### Custom Thanksgiving place cards and name cards


A name card is a small way to give every guest a warm welcome. Make folded cardstock cards for a classic look, or cut leaf shapes that rest on a plate or wrap around a napkin.


For cardstock name cards, add a shape and each guest’s name in Design Space. Choose a writing font, set the name to Draw instead of Cut, and Attach it to the card shape so the writing stays in position when you make the project. If your card requires folding, don’t forget to add a Score line in Design Space to make folding super simple and precise. Cut the cards with your Cricut cutting machine, following the directions on Design Space, then fold or assemble them as needed.

### Thanksgiving placemats


Custom placemats give each seat its own little moment. Add an iron-on design to fabric placemats, or cut out paper placemats for a more unique shape and intricate details. For iron-on elements added to fabric placemats, be sure to keep names and decorative phrases near the edges so they remain visible around the plate.


[Flower Bud Place Mat](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/57563e41ee508efa4332322a)


Cricut


[Give Thanks Placemat](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/59dfa06767cbc86ae7476158)


At the kids’ table, make paper coloring placemats with outline turkeys, leaves, tic-tac-toe grids, and an “I’m thankful for…” prompt. Use a compatible Cricut pen to draw the designs, sizing the paper to your machine’s supported drawing area. Set out crayons so little guests can decorate their own place at the table. Find more family projects and links to kids’ placemats you can make with your Cricut cutting machine in our[Thanksgiving crafts guide](https://cricut.com/blog/guide-to-thanksgiving-crafts/) .


### Thanksgiving table runners


A runner if a great way to add some personality and a seasonal theme to the table without covering the whole surface. Add “Give Thanks” or some seasonal images to a compatible fabric runner using iron-on. Position the phrase near an end so serving dishes and the centerpiece won’t hide it, and sprinkle any fun and simple images and motifs across the edges.


Prefer a painted finish? Cut a stencil with your Cricut machine, apply it to a suitable runner, and use fabric paint according to its instructions. Test the stencil and paint on a scrap or on the backside of the runner first to check for bleeding.

If you’re using iron-on material, don’t forget to make sure you have the Mirror option turned on before cutting and follow the[Cricut Heat Guide](https://cricut.com/heatguide) for your material and heat press settings.


### Napkin rings, glass tags, and favors


You can use leftover cardstock to make leaf-topped napkin bands and matching glass tags. Cut a strip long enough to wrap around a folded napkin, secure the ends, and add a leaf or other shape that fits your theme with each person’s name written by your Cricut cutting machine. For stemmed glasses, make tags with an opening and slit that fit around the stem.


You can also personalize the outside of glassware with permanent vinyl names or small fall designs. Keep decals below the rim and away from food-contact surfaces, and follow the vinyl’s application and care instructions.

## Thanksgiving Table Decor Ideas by Style


Start with the colors and textures already in your home, then choose a few decorative embellishments you can make with Cricut. Remember, you don’t need to make a whole lot of décor pieces for your table spread! Two or three coordinated details are enough to carry a style across the table.


### Classic rustic Thanksgiving table


Pair wood, burlap, and natural textures with warm cream, burnt orange, or brown accents. Personalize smooth wood slices with vinyl names, cut cardstock leaves for napkin rings, and add a small vinyl-lettered wood sign at the center. Let the grain of the wood and the woven runner provide most of the texture.


### Farmhouse Thanksgiving table


Use neutral linens and simple greenery as the base (natural or paper are both good). Make cream cardstock place cards and menus with dark lettering and finish with green paper napkin wraps and leaf cut-outs to lay under the menus. Repeat the same font on the menus and name cards for a coordinated finish.


### Blue and white Thanksgiving table


Bring together white pumpkins, blue patterns, touches of gold and white accents, and eucalyptus for a fresh fall palette. Cut blue and white place cards, make white cardstock napkin rings with blue accents, and add matching blue glass tags. Keep the handmade details simple so they sit comfortably alongside patterned dishes or linens.


For more ways to combine linens, dishes, and handmade accents, explore our blog on[creating the perfect dinner party tablescape](https://cricut.com/blog/dinner-party-tablescape-inspiration/) .


## Add a Thanksgiving Centerpiece


Once your place settings are ready, bring the middle of the table together with pumpkins, paper foliage, or a handmade arrangement. Choose colors and incorporate visual motifs and shapes that match your place cards or runner. For more ideas, explore our[Thanksgiving centerpiece ideas](https://cricut.com/blog/showstopping-diy-thanksgiving-table-centerpieces/) blog to find a project that fits your table.


## Best Cricut Materials for Thanksgiving Table Projects


Choose your material based on the surface you’re decorating and how you plan to use the finished piece.


- **Cardstock:** Use for folded place cards, cut leaf shapes, paper napkin rings, glass tags, and favor boxes. Choose printable cardstock when making printed name cards. Cardstock is thicker and heavier than normal copy or kraft paper, which makes your pieces feel more professional and polished.
- **Iron-on vinyl:** Use to personalize compatible fabric runners, placemats, napkins, and tea towels. Follow the heat settings and care instructions for your fabric and iron-on combination.
- **Permanent vinyl:** Use it for designs on the outside of glassware and other suitable smooth surfaces. Don’t forget to use transfer tape to keep small pieces in place and to keep the vinyl design from stretching during application!
- **Wood blanks:** Use purchased blanks for small table signs, name plaques, and place-card holders. Apply vinyl or iron-on lettering to a smooth, prepared surface. As a note, these projects don’t require your machine to cut wood, only vinyl or iron-on material. If you’d like to engrave or cut thin pieces of wood as accents to your table, you will need a[Cricut Maker®](https://cricut.com/en-us/cutting-machines/cricut-maker) .


Before you begin, check your machine’s material and tool compatibility. Our guide on[how to pick the right Cricut material for your project](https://cricut.com/blog/how-to-pick-the-right-cricut-material-for-your-project/) explains when to choose iron-on or adhesive vinyl.

## Thanksgiving Table Decor FAQs


####


The best Thanksgiving table decor makes guests feel welcome while leaving room for the meal. Start with a runner, personalized place cards, and a simple centerpiece. Repeat a few colors or shapes across the table to bring everything together.


####


Choose a palette, lay down your table linens, and add place settings. Make one personalized item for each guest, such as a name card or glass tag, then finish with a centerpiece. Add favors or extra paper details if there’s room.


####


Layer a runner or tablecloth, placemats, plates and flatware, napkins and napkin rings, glassware and glass tags, and place cards. Add the centerpiece last, checking that it leaves space for dishes and clear views across the table. For a step-by-step guide, check out our[Thanksgiving table setting and decor blog](https://cricut.com/blog/thanksgiving-crafts-with-cricut/) .


####


Create a card shape and add a guest’s name in Design Space. Use a writing font with the text set to Draw, then Attach the name to the card shape before making it to keep the writing in place on the card. Use a compatible Cricut pen and blade to write and cut the cardstock. Fold or assemble the finished card and repeat for each guest.


####


Cut folded cards or leaf shapes from cardstock and add handwritten names. For a different look, attach a paper name tag to a small pumpkin or place it in a wood-slice holder. With a Cricut cutting machine, you can cut matching shapes and add names using a compatible pen, cut vinyl, or Print Then Cut on a supported machine.


####


A 12-by-18-inch rectangle is a useful starting point for an adult fabric placemat, but measure your plates and table before choosing a size. Leave room between settings. For paper placemats made with Cricut, check your cutting machine’s supported cut or draw area and size the design to fit. A full-size fabric placemat can be decorated with a smaller iron-on design even if you have a smaller Cricut cutting machine.


####


Use cardstock for place cards and paper details, iron-on for compatible fabric linens, and permanent vinyl for the outside of glassware. Purchased wood blanks work well for signs and place-card holders decorated with vinyl lettering. Always check material, tool, and machine compatibility.
